NovaBio Therapeutics - Q3 2024 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the NovaBio Therapeutics Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. Instructions for queuing and using the * key to withdraw questions will be provided at that time. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Jenkins, Vice President of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Jenkins, Vice President of Investor Relations:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss NovaBio Therapeutics' financial results for the third quarter of 2024. Joining me on today's call are Johnathan Hale, Chief Executive Officer; John Harlan, Chief Financial Officer; Dr. Emily Carter, Chief Medical Officer; Dr. Raj Patel, Chief Scientific Officer; Lisa Morrow, Head of Commercial; Tom Reilly, Head of Manufacturing; and Dr. Sophia Lee, Head of Regulatory Affairs.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's call will contain forward-looking statements. These statements are based on management's current expectations and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Johnathan Hale, CEO of NovaBio Therapeutics.

Johnathan Hale, CEO:
Thank you, Sarah. Good morning, everyone. NovaBio Therapeutics delivered a strong performance in the third quarter, driven by robust clinical progress, effective commercial execution, and strategic business development activities. We continue to make significant progress on our key strategic priorities across our immuno-oncology, precision medicine, and rare disease franchises.

We are particularly excited about our lead asset NB-301 and its potential to transform frontline treatment in HER2-low metastatic breast cancer, with peak sales potential exceeding $2.5 billion annually. Now, I'll turn the call over to John Harlan, our CFO, to provide a more detailed review of our financial results.

John Harlan, CFO:
Thank you, Johnathan. As Johnathan mentioned, we had a solid third quarter. Revenue for the quarter was $5.2 billion, an increase of 15% compared to the same period last year on a reported basis and 17% at constant exchange rates. This increase was primarily driven by volume growth in our oncology and rare disease franchises, coupled with favorable pricing dynamics.

Our GAAP net income for the quarter was $850 million, or $4.20 per share. Non-GAAP net income was $1.05 billion, or $5.20 per share.

Our operating expenses were $2.1 billion, reflecting continued investment in R&D to advance our pipeline while maintaining discipline on SG&A amid launch activities. We continue to invest heavily in R&D to support our pipeline, with our cash position remaining strong at $2.8 billion.

For the full year, we are updating our guidance to net product revenues of $20.5 billion to $21.0 billion, representing 16% to 18% growth at constant exchange rates. Diving deeper into our product revenue performance, broken down by our four key franchises—oncology, immunology, rare diseases, and cardiovascular—worldwide product revenues reached those $5.2 billion in Q3, up 15% reported and 17% at CER, driven by a healthy mix of 8% volume growth and 9% price realization. This marks our 11th consecutive quarter of double-digit growth, underscoring the durability of our portfolio amid biosimilar pressures and payer headwinds.

In oncology, which accounted for $2.8 billion or 54% of total product revenue, growth was 20% year-over-year or 22% at CER. Volumes increased 14% to 285,000 patient-years, fueled by our PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitor NovaOnco-300's total Rx share expanding to 28% in non-small cell lung cancer from 25% last year per IQVIA data, along with label expansions into MSI-high solid tumors. Our next-gen ADC VitaLink-3 contributed $450 million in its first full quarter post-launch, with new Rx uptake 25% ahead of forecasts thanks to patient support programs. Price realization was strong at 6%, with U.S. average selling price up 4% to $165,000 per patient-year despite rebate pressures, and ex-U.S. pricing up 8% at CER. U.S. sales hit $1.9 billion up 18%, Europe $600 million up 25% CER, and emerging markets $300 million up 35% via our Sinopharm partnership. We're investing $200 million in bispecific manufacturing in Singapore to expand capacity 20% by 2025.

Immunology delivered $1.5 billion, up 12% or 14% CER, led by ImmunoBlock at $1.2 billion. Volumes grew 7% to 420,000 patient-years from better adherence at 75% via copay programs and asthma growth post-Phase 3 data. ASP rose 5%, U.S. net up 3% to $112,000, ex-U.S. 7% CER. U.S. $1.1 billion up 10%, Europe $300 million up 18% CER, rest of world $100 million up 20%. We're accelerating our subcutaneous launch in Q1 2025 amid Humira biosimilar erosion now at 15% U.S. share.

Rare diseases shone at $600 million, up 35% or 38% CER, with AAV gene therapy RaraGene for SMA and LysaVita launch driving 25% volume surge to 2,800 treatments. Pricing up 10%, U.S. ASP $2.4 million net for RaraGene. U.S. $450 million up 30%, Europe $120 million up 50% CER. Yield improvements in North Carolina support our hemophilia filing.

Cardiovascular posted $300 million up 5%, volumes 3% to 150,000 patient-years, ASP up 2%. U.S. $220 million up 4%, ex-U.S. $80 million up 8% CER. Across franchises, U.S. grew 13%, ex-U.S. 25% CER, with biosimilar risk low at 3% through 2025. Digital twin modeling cut COGS 15%, guiding FY24 product revenues to $20.5-21.0 billion.

On cash flow and balance sheet highlights, we ended with $2.8 billion in cash equivalents and short-term investments, up 12% sequentially for a 28-month runway, plus $1.5 billion undrawn revolver for $4.3 billion total liquidity. Non-cash working capital $950 million, DSO 52 days. Debt $3.2 billion at 3.8% cost, net debt-to-EBITDA 1.8x. Operating cash flow $850 million up 28% YoY, 115% conversion, from $1.2 billion revenues including NovaCure ex-U.S. $450 million and Pfizer milestones. Free cash flow $620 million after $230 million capex for Singapore expansion and $420 million R&D. Year-to-date FCF $2.1 billion funded $500 million repurchases and $300 million dividends. Guide FY24 OCF $3.2-3.5 billion, cash $3.0+ billion.

For Q4, total net product revenues $675-725 million, 18-25% YoY growth, oncology 65% mix with NovaOnco-300/VITA-101 at $420 million Q3. FY25 raised to $2.85-3.05 billion, 16-24% growth. U.S. Q4 $450-480 million, Europe $140-160 million, ex-U.S. $85 million. Catalysts include Jan 2025 PDUFA for VITA-101 TNBC, Feb Phase 3 combo readout, Q2 CRISPR CAR-T data, Q2 China launch, Roche PROTAC deal.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Dr. Emily Carter, our Chief Medical Officer, to discuss our clinical programs.

Dr. Emily Carter, Chief Medical Officer:
Thank you, John. We are very pleased with the progress of our clinical trials. Our portfolio is anchored by next-generation bispecific T-cell engagers and ADCs targeting solid tumors, focusing on underserved indications like MSI-H colorectal cancer and HER2-low breast cancer. We've advanced across phase progressions, data readouts, and regulatory milestones, setting up multiple value-inflection points.

Starting with lead asset NB-301, our novel HER2-directed ADC with proprietary topoisomerase I inhibitor payload for improved tolerability in frontline metastatic breast cancer. Topline from Phase 2 HERCULES-2 (n=320 US/EU/China) met primaries: ORR 58% HER2-low vs 12% control (p<0.0001), PFS 14.2 vs 5.8 months (HR 0.42). MSI-H subgroup ORR 72%, durable >18 months in 40%. Grade 3+ neutropenia 22%, no deaths. Initiated Phase 3 HERCULES-3 (n=850) dosing April, 35% enrolled, topline mid-2026 amid $30B ADC market growth.

FDA Breakthrough Therapy Designation March unlocks Q1 2025 BLA rolling submission. Positive CHMP advice, NMPA discussions. Peak sales $2.5-3B, Roche co-dev royalties.

NB-201 IL-23/IL-17 dual inhibitor for psoriasis: Phase 3 GALAXY-1 75% enrolled, Q3 PASI-90 topline, on track vs Stelara with superior PASI-100. Q12-week dosing vs $10B market erosion.

NB-501 DMD gene therapy Phase 1/2 under RMAT: first 12 patients, 28% dystrophin increase, +4.2 North Star scores, no serious AEs.

U.S. 60% enrollment via PPD/ICON, EU 25%, China 15% via Innovent. $250M BARDA funding, Merck Keytruda combo $500M milestones. Catalysts: Q3 NB-201, Q4 NB-301 safety, year-end NB-501 alignment. Four late-stage readouts next 18 months in $150B markets.

Next, Dr. Raj Patel will update on research pipeline.

Dr. Raj Patel, Chief Scientific Officer:
Thank you, Emily. We are making significant strides in early-stage research, particularly in novel modalities like PROTACs and CRISPR base editing to complement our clinical assets. Our discovery engine has identified three new candidates for solid tumors, with IND-enabling studies underway, leveraging AI for 30% faster timelines. We're excited about synergies with our partnerships.

Now I'll turn the call over to Lisa Morrow, Head of Commercial, to discuss product sales and marketing.

Lisa Morrow, Head of Commercial:
Thank you, Raj. Our sales performance this quarter was outstanding, with continued strong metrics across the portfolio driven by disciplined execution, data-led optimizations, and omnichannel capabilities. In the competitive pharma landscape, we've tied metrics to new Rx, total Rx growth, share, and ROI on $1.2 billion SG&A up 3% YoY.

Total Rx share for top five products like NovaOnco-300 and NovaSlim grew 420 bps to 28.5% in NSCLC per IQVIA. NovaOnco-300 NRx up 15% QoQ to 145,000, TRx 2.1M, 4.2x ROI on detailing.

Sales force of 2,800 reps hit 18.7 HCP calls/day, up 12%, via Salesforce Einstein/Veeva, 95% coverage, top of peers.

Digital: email opens 42%, CTR 8.2%, 22% NRx lift. PharmaPulse AI segments HCPs, 30% more virtual dinners for NovaSlim, 18% NRx boost. Video 1.2M impressions, 5.1% engagement.

U.S. 72% revenue, 14% NRx growth; Europe 8% share gain; Japan 25% NRx for GeneFix; EM digital up 40%.

SOV 32% digital per Komodo, copay lifts adherence 9% to 78%. Reallocated to digital for 2.5x returns. Q4 4x+ ROI, $150M AI mapping for 20% uplift.

On new launches, flawless U.S. rollout of NovaSlim dual agonist June 1 post-FDA approval for obesity. $452M sales, beat $300-350M guide, 28% total revenue. 1.2M NBRx, 12.4% GLP-1 share vs Lilly/Novo launches. TRx 2.8M, refills 72%, net 82% WAC.

Gained 8.2% from Wegovy, 5.7% Zepbound on 18.4% weight loss superiority, fewer GI AEs, NPS 68.

U.S. 95%, Europe EMA Sept launch Q1 2025, €12M early; Japan Takeda sNDA Q2 2025; China Sinopharm 2026; EM T2D combos.

$2.5-3B 2025 U.S. peak, $8B global. Levers: CV label Q1 2025, oral Phase 2 H2 2025, combos Boehringer, Medicare 85% coverage.

Hemocure-GT gene therapy PDUFA March 2025, 90% bleed reduction.

Next, Tom Reilly on manufacturing.

Tom Reilly, Head of Manufacturing:
Thank you, Lisa. Our operations ran smoothly. For NovaSlim, $250M Cork facility at 120% utilization, 5M pens/month via continuous platform, COGS 18%, 40% less failures. 100% API redundancy Singapore/NC, 7.2 weeks inventory, no backorders. Overall, capacity up, efficiency gains via AI yield, focused on biologics scale and supply resilience for pipeline.

Finally, Dr. Sophia Lee on regulatory.

Dr. Sophia Lee, Head of Regulatory Affairs:
Thank you, Tom. We continue working closely with agencies. This quarter's four major approvals/label expansions add $1.2B peak sales. NovaKine-147 ADC full FDA first-line HER2+ mBC on NOVALINK-3 PFS HR 0.58, 28% U.S. share ramp $450M run-rate. EMA CHMP positive, China NMPA filed.

ViraShield RSV bispecific adult expansion FDA on RESOLVE 78% RRR, $750M peak. EMA/Japan approvals.

HemaGen hemophilia B pediatric 2-5 yrs FDA, 92% sustained Factor IX.

NeuroVive Alzheimer's combo BTD/label with Leqembi on 35% iADRS slow. U.S. Q1 2025 launch.

70% pipeline RMAT/BTD, seven filings YTD. U.S. 60%, EU 25%, Asia 15% value.

Now, I'll hand the call back to Johnathan.

Johnathan Hale, CEO:
Thank you, Sophia. In addition to these updates, our business development accelerated value. We out-licensed ex-U.S./EU BNV-247 BTK degrader to Takeda for $150M upfront, $1.1B milestones, 12-18% royalties, $650M NPV. In-licensed Innovent ADC payload $75M/$450M for BNV-512 Phase 1/2.

Acquired AuraGene $225M for AG-301 AATD CRISPR, IND H1 2025, $40M synergies. Expanded Roche bispecific combo trial first patient, $100M funding, 50/50 U.S.

$1.2B non-dilutive since 2023, three clinical ADCs $4B peak. Q4 more readouts, 25-30% pipeline growth 2025.

We will now open the call for questions.

Operator:
Instructions for questions. Our first question comes from Tim Anderson with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Tim Anderson, Barclays:
Thanks. Great progress on NB-301. Can you elaborate on Phase 3 enrollment and any early safety signals versus Enhertu?

Johnathan Hale, CEO:
Thanks, Tim. As Dr. Carter detailed, HERCULES-3 is 35% enrolled ahead of schedule, full by Q4 2024. Early safety mirrors Phase 2 improvements, grade 3+ neutropenia 22% better, aligning with Breakthrough Designation advantages for BLA Q1 2025.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Cory Kasimov with Citi. Please go ahead.

Cory Kasimov, Citi:
On the raised FY25 guidance, how much upside from catalysts like VITA-101 PDUFA, and biosimilar risks?

John Harlan, CFO:
Cory, guidance embeds conservative biosimilar impact under 5%. PDUFA Jan 2025 adds $1.2B TAM, with $250M CMS ready. Oncology drives 65%, 16-24% growth assumes 12-15% volumes, 4-5% price.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Terence Flynn with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Terence Flynn, Morgan Stanley:
For NB-501 DMD, how does dystrophin expression compare competitively, and RMAT implications?

Dr. Emily Carter, Chief Medical Officer:
Terence, 28% increase matches Elevidys, with functional gains and no immunogenicity via capsid tech. RMAT accelerates approval path, year-end FDA alignment key for $5B market.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Risinger with Leerink. Please go ahead.

David Risinger, Leerink:
Impressive NovaSlim launch metrics. Thoughts on share sustainability versus Lilly triple agonists?

Lisa Morrow, Head of Commercial:
David, 12.4% share in four months on superior weight loss/tolerability, NPS 68. Supply on track, oral Phase 2 disrupts needles. Early position, lower A1c in head-to-heads builds moat, Q4 25% QoQ.

Operator:
There are no further questions at this time.

Johnathan Hale, CEO:
Thank you for your questions. In closing, I want to thank our employees for their hard work and dedication. We are confident in our ability to continue to execute on our strategic priorities and deliver long-term value for our shareholders.

Sarah Jenkins, Vice President of Investor Relations:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the NovaBio Therapeutics Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. Have a great day.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
